actual_facts: Windows stores the complete directory deny as one effective ACE (flags 0x00, mask 0x00130156) plus one inherit-only recursive ACE (flags 0x0b, mask 0x40130156; mapped 0x00130156). Repeating the current repair duplicates both ACEs.

Windows stores the complete explicit file deny with flags 0x00. Repeating the current repair duplicates it. The current exact-flags-0x03 single-ACE predicate does not recognize either valid stored form.

Outside and protected-directory ordinary writes fail with OS error 5; full reads succeed. DELETE_CHILD-only opens succeed, including a directory with the complete capability deny. Adding FILE_WRITE_DATA to DELETE_CHILD fails.
Outside file/directory and protected .git are actually deleted. Authorized workspace/temp create/delete operations succeed.

DELETE-only opens outside/protected paths succeed, but partial-root DELETE itself is denied. These observations do not justify claiming every DELETE path skips restriction: parent DELETE_CHILD remains an alternate authorization route.
conclusions: Two real independent defects remain: native ACE normalization breaks idempotence, and write-restricted capability enforcement does not block parent DELETE_CHILD sufficiently to enforce the promised workspace-only deletion scope.
A safe ACE fix must preserve effective and recursively inherited deny coverage, distinguish file scope using a stable target identity, and retain all missing-right/scope/order negatives.
Removing WRITE_RESTRICTED or accepting broad identity restricting SIDs would alter the full-read/authorization contract. No such production change has been made.
The diagnostic job success proves complete observations only. Original permission tests and full sandbox semantics remain open.
